synopsis: The booklet lists MIL-STD-3022 among standards and guides spanning multiple domains in its discussion of when simulation can be trusted [f8154]. The glossary describes it as a US Department of Defense standard and template for documenting verification, validation and accreditation (VV&A) of models and simulations [f14663, f14653]. However, Chapter 10 explicitly says MIL-STD-3022 was not verified, and the glossary repeats that gap alongside DO-178C and DO-330 [f7719, f14664]. Planners should therefore distinguish the booklet’s description of the standard’s role from verification of the standard itself [f14663, f7719, f14664].

relations.note: Both explicitly report that MIL-STD-3022 was not verified.
Both identify its US defense role in documenting model VV&A.
The glossary specifies the purpose of a standard listed in Chapter 10.
The verification gap qualifies the standard’s inclusion in the cross-domain list.
The glossary qualifies its definition by disclosing that the standard was not verified.
